newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU tells marine insurers more competition needed.
newsitem.headline: EU tells marine insurers more competition needed.

text.p: The European Commission took aim at the world largest group of marine insurers on Thursday, telling them that the rules they had agreed among themselves contradicted European Union competition law.

It said Karel Van Miert, its antitrust commissioner, had written to the International Group of P&I Clubs saying it must foster more competition among its members if it was to be granted an exemption from EU rules.
The group is an association representing some 89 percent of the worldwide market for P&I (protection and indemnity) marine insurance.
In a statement the Commission said it believed the group was restricting competition in the industry in two ways.
First, its rules obliged all P&I Clubs to offer the same level of insurance cover to shippers even if a large number of ship owners wished to obtain substantially lower terms than those offered.
This had been the subject of a complaint from the Greek Shipping Cooperation Committee, which in part triggered the EU executive's probe, the Commission said.
Secondly, the Commission said the groups' rules imposed limits on price competition between insurers grouped in P&I clubs.
The Commission noted that it had exempted some of these limits in 1985, but that this had not proved sufficient.
"The price limits cannot be exempted as they stand today," the Commission said.
P&I insurance covers shipowners against liabilities for such damages as oil pollution, crew or passenger injury and collisions with other vessels.
The Commission said the international group allows clubs of P&I insurers to share claims from shipowners above a certain amount.
It had been exempted from competition from EU rules for 10 years but an investigation afterwards had led to the current finding.
